issues: Whether incentive plan or bonus payments that would have vested during the notice period are recoverable as part of damages for wrongful dismissal
Whether an 'actively employed' condition in an incentive plan constitutes a valid forfeiture clause that precludes recovery of the payment as part of common law damages
Whether a court will read down or deem satisfied an 'actively employed' condition for the purpose of calculating the damages period
The distinction between a contractual entitlement to a bonus and a claim for the bonus as part of the damages package for wrongful dismissal
Mitigation of damages: whether the employee's duty to mitigate includes seeking new employment with a comparable incentive plan
key_facts: long-term incentive plan with a payout date falling within the notice period
plan requires 'actively employed' status to qualify
employee seeks the LTIP payout as part of his damages
causes_of_action: breach of contract (implied duty to provide reasonable notice)
candidate_statutes: Employment Standards Act (provincial — sets the statutory floor for notice; the common law claim is the operative one here)
search_terms: bonus recoverable as part of damages
needs_clarification: Which province or territory governs the employment relationship? (The common law of wrongful dismissal and any applicable employment standards legislation are provincial.)
